title: O-01d0 polar-fibre structural reductions
oneLine: Exact polar-fibre and Hermite reductions, four rejected proof architectures, and a four-gate executable handoff sharpen an open all-index transversality problem.
abstract: This anonymous, unrefereed candidate studies the internal O-01d0 target: whether a four-generator weighted-homogeneous ideal has empty weighted-projective zero locus for every index n at least 6. It proves a fixed-index properness and finite-freeness criterion, reduces the lower balanced obstruction to triple coprimality for an explicit Hermite family, and supplies exact incidence, squarefreeness, confluent-boundary, exceptional-fibre-avoidance, and fifth-derivative connection results. Producer evidence gives fixed-index consequences at n=21 and 25; n=29 is sealed but not rerun. Exact computations reject bounded scalar transfer, a canonical monic remainder tail, degree-at-most-twelve projective transfer, and the claim that every structural window prime works for the upper determinant. Large bounded scans support, but do not prove, a narrower pair-content and four-factor conjecture. O-01d0 remains open and unfalsified. The release does not prove AF5 transversality or any linked headline conjecture, and it has no independent reconstruction, formal verification, specialist review, editorial peer review, or priority determination.
narration: O-01d0 is a precise algebraic gate inside a programme connected to the Polydegree Conjecture. It asks whether four weighted homogeneous polynomials have no common projective zero for every index from six onward. This release does not answer that question. It records what can now be proved, what has been falsified, and exactly what remains. A fixed-index theorem shows why one geometrically empty polar fibre would force a complete intersection that is finite free over its deformation parameter. Producer computations supply such fixed-index consequences at twenty-one and twenty-five. A third case, twenty-nine, is preserved by a sealed source-and-transcript record but is not rerun. The main structural step rewrites the lower arithmetic obstruction as triple coprimality for three consecutive members of an explicit one-variable Hermite family. The paper proves that any structural triple gcd is squarefree, controls two exceptional boundary fibres, and derives a fifth-derivative connection whose reciprocal form has only five boundary columns. Several attractive shortcuts fail exactly. Low-degree scalar transfer, a canonical polynomial-remainder tail, bounded-degree projective transfer, and the claim that every prime in the structural window works are all rejected by reproducible counterevidence. Large finite scans point instead to a pair-content and four-factor theorem, but finite survival is not a proof. The remaining route has four independent gates: that lower theorem, one simultaneous good prime for the upper determinant, graded multiplier lifts in both odd residue classes, and a complete projective chart cover. Ordinary and optimized producer replay agree, public continuous integration passes, and GitHub and Zenodo expose matching assets. Those facts establish availability and internal replay, not O-01d0, AF5 transversality, any linked conjecture, independent reproduction, formal verification, specialist review, peer review, novelty, priority, or impact. This synthetic-voice briefing is a communication aid, not mathematical evidence.

keyResults: A finite-dimensional fixed-index polar fibre implies a regular sequence and finite freeness over the deformation parameter, with explicit rank (n-1)n(n+1)(n+2)/24.
The lower balanced obstruction is reduced to triple coprimality for J_A, J_(A+5), and J_(A+10); structural triple gcds are proved squarefree.

Uniform confluent initial forms, joint avoidance of the critical and first infinity-collision fibres, and an exact fifth-derivative A+20-to-A connection constrain the remaining Hermite boundary problem.
Four tempting proof architectures are rejected exactly, including the universal all-window-prime upper determinant claim.
Bounded pair-content scans through A=3000 and primes below 12000 support a narrower four-factor conjecture but do not establish it.
evidence: A 14-page manuscript and accessible Markdown; 20 indexed claims and non-claims; 13 experiment records with stopping rules and exclusions; 12 portable and 6 PassageMath/Sage checks replayed in ordinary and optimized modes with all 18 paired output hashes identical; fixed-index transcripts at n=21 and n=25 plus a sealed, not-rerun n=29 record; exact counterexamples and hostile controls; a 147-entry manifest; pinned environment files; a five-role producer-coordinated internal review, ten-item repair record, and bounded confirmation; public CI on Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13; and byte-matched GitHub and Zenodo assets. These establish availability, internal replay, integrity, exact finite statements in their declared domains, and internal editorial closure—not the open uniform theorem or independent mathematical validation.
statusDetail: Anonymous, unrefereed structural-reductions candidate with internal PASS_WITH_NOTES. Written proofs and computer-assisted all-index statements are supplied for specialist checking; finite computations retain their exact bounds. The n=21 and n=25 producer transcripts replay, while n=29 is sealed and source-bound but not rerun. O-01d0 remains open and unfalsified. No unaffiliated rerun, independent implementation, proof-assistant formalization, external specialist review, journal peer review, absolute novelty or priority determination, or impact evaluation has occurred.

openProblems: Prove or falsify the pair-content and four-factor theorem controlling denominator-valid adjacent-pair content and the third-row same-root event.
Prove that every index admits at least one structural prime that simultaneously avoids the lower exceptions and makes the upper two-level determinant nonzero.
Construct degree- and (x3,x4)-compatible graded multiplier lifts in both odd residue classes.
Assemble the affine and residual charts into a complete projective-emptiness proof, or isolate a counterexample.
Obtain an unaffiliated specialist reconstruction and a separately authored implementation while preserving corrections as versioned successors.

semanticBridge.description: The package maps weighted-projective emptiness through a fixed-index properness criterion and two-level degeneration to triple coprimality of J_A sections, separates lower, upper, multiplier, and chart-cover gates, and indexes the exact scope and evidence of every positive and negative claim.
remainingRisks: The written reductions and computer-assisted all-index squarefreeness theorem have not been independently reconstructed by specialists.
Bounded pair-content survival can miss a later nonlinear common factor or an exceptional prime outside the scan.
The n=29 fixed-index record is sealed rather than rerun.
The lower and upper prime choices, multiplier lifts, and residual projective charts have not been assembled into uniform emptiness.

humanJudgmentGates: Check each written polar-fibre and Hermite reduction as mathematics rather than inferring it from successful replay.

Keep one bad structural prime separate from failure of the one-good-prime route.
Require a proved graded multiplier map and all-chart cover before promoting local or residue-class calculations to O-01d0.
Require external specialist assessment before any target-conjecture, first, priority, or field-acceptance language.
